reason: Conversation 1 opens with the stop-using and unplug instruction, then asks sensible follow-ups (which switch trips, freestanding or built-in, age). It gives a ranked diagnosis that matches the ground truth (HV parts or the door interlock), warns against opening the case, and gives an honest repair-versus-replace verdict. It also advises an electrician if the circuit still trips with the microwave out of the picture and gives WEEE disposal advice. Its weaknesses are overconfidence in the HV-component/magnetron diagnosis and no direct ask about the extension lead or another circuit. Conversation 2 has the right safety stop and escalation but is a single terse turn with no diagnosis, no questions, no repair-or-replace guidance and no explanation of why, so it is much less useful to the homeowner.
